column1: # OpenBSD pledge(2) promise  ->  Darwin seatbelt (sandbox_init(3)) translation
#   1 promise    the pledge keyword as it appears in tool sources
#   3 seatbelt   rule fragment spliced into the generated profile
#   4 notes      why a downgrade is acceptable / what to watch for
# "partial" means the seatbelt rule is broader or narrower than the kernel check
# pledge() performs. abzu-compat.c logs any partial/unsupported promise and fails
# closed unless ABZU_PLEDGE=off -- see docs/OPENBSD-DIFFS.md section B1.

column4: notes
tty ioctl spelling differs; validated against Darwin getty
plain read-path promise, exact match
needs a per-tool writable root; default /var/tmp/%TOOL%
Darwin /tmp symlinks to /private/tmp - both required
concrete paths normally come from unveil()
Mach-O needs explicit executable-page mapping
directly expressible
no execve-without-fork distinction on Mach-O
legacy seatbelt form; bind ports narrowed per tool
BSD send/recv signal promotion has no seatbelt analogue; log + fail
multicast needs the NetworkExtension backend (roadmap R-014)
/dev/pf does not exist on XNU; patch the caller out (see import/skip.txt)
resolver-only narrowing, not general network
OpenDirectory lookups touch more than master.passwd
routing socket flags differ; prefer Darwin route(8)
signal plus proc_info family
ps(1)-style introspection only
IOKit audio client access
pair with stdio; ioctl whitelist is per-literal on Darwin
device enumeration differs from ugen(4)
too broad for shipping; list literals per tool instead
xattr/flags semantics differ on HFS+/APFS
O_CREAT-denial heuristic cannot be expressed; documented downgrade
